criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both use an oblique isometric projection with diagonal ground axes.
Industrial structures and transmission towers are viewed from a consistent elevated yaw.
different: CANDIDATE framing is consistently wider and more top-down, with smaller facilities and longer visible road runs.
REFERENCE crops feel tighter and lower, emphasizing large foreground textures and silhouettes.

evidence.observation: Tight oblique framing gives the plant, pole, and diagonal road large screen presence.
The matching crop presents a broader, flatter map area with much smaller equipment.
Large factory masses and close ground framing dominate the crop.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both use charcoal industrial structures, dark ground, sparse amber lights, and cyan accents.
Warm-state crops retain a brown soil-and-metal palette in both boards.
different: REFERENCE has stronger embossed microtexture, warmer midtones, and cohesive edge highlights.
CANDIDATE surfaces are darker and flatter, with repetitive parcel lines and a more uniform brown wash.

evidence.observation: Roofs, concrete, roads, and soil carry dense relief detail with integrated amber highlights.
The factory shares the charcoal-and-amber palette but sits on flatter, lower-contrast terrain.
Warm rocky soil has articulated stones, tonal variation, and bright metallic towers.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both shift from a dark neutral upper row to a warm brown middle row while retaining the industrial kit.
Transmission towers, factories, and route accents remain recognizable across the visible state changes.
different: REFERENCE ends in a diffuse olive-amber territory haze, while CANDIDATE returns to crisp charcoal terrain with blue water and bright cyan routing.
CANDIDATE's warm state reads as a broad uniform tint; REFERENCE integrates the warmth into terrain and local lighting.

evidence.observation: Warm ground and lighting preserve the same tower-and-road world language.
The same industrial assets persist under a broad brown environmental tint.
The lower-row world is softened by an olive-amber haze and translucent route coverage.
